QuestionStmt.S: The maximum value and minimum value of the volume of the parallelepiped having coterminous edges $\hat{i} + x\hat{j} + \hat{k}$, $\hat{j} + x\hat{k}$ and $x\hat{i} + \hat{k}$ are respectively

Solution.S:
Let
$$\vec{a} = \hat{i} + x\hat{j} + \hat{k}$$
$$\vec{b} = \hat{j} + x\hat{k}$$
$$\vec{c} = x\hat{i} + \hat{k}$$

Volume of parallelepiped is given by the scalar triple product:

$$V = |[\vec{a}\,\vec{b}\,\vec{c}]| = \left| \begin{vmatrix} 1 & x & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & x \\ x & 0 & 1 \end{vmatrix} \right|$$

Expanding the determinant:
$$= 1(1 - 0) - x(0 - x^2) + 1(0 - x)$$
$$= 1 + x^3 - x$$

So, $f(x) = x^3 - x + 1$.

For maxima/minima, differentiate with respect to $x$:
$$f'(x) = 3x^2 - 1$$

Set $f'(x) = 0$:
$$3x^2 - 1 = 0 \Rightarrow x = \pm \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$$

Second derivative: $f''(x) = 6x$.

At $x = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$: $f'' > 0$ → minimum.
At $x = -\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$: $f'' < 0$ → maximum.

Now, evaluate $f(x)$ at these points:

Maximum value:
$$f\left(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) = 1 + \left(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)^3 - \left(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) = 1 - \frac{1}{3\sqrt{3}} + \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = 1 + \frac{2}{3\sqrt{3}}$$

Minimum value:
$$f\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) = 1 + \left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)^3 - \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = 1 + \frac{1}{3\sqrt{3}} - \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = 1 - \frac{2}{3\sqrt{3}}$$

Thus, the maximum and minimum values are $1 + \frac{2}{3\sqrt{3}}$ and $1 - \frac{2}{3\sqrt{3}}$ respectively.

$$\boxed{\text{Option B}}$$
